# truefoundry_gateway_guardrails_policy (Resource)

Manages one named AI gateway guardrail policy on control plane v0.179+. Multiple policies coexist; every matching policy runs. Replaces one rule of the deprecated `truefoundry_gateway_guardrails_config`: map the rule's `id` to `name` and keep its other fields. Model targets require an LLM input or output guardrail; MCP targets require a pre- or post-invoke guardrail. Import by policy name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One named policy per target region; policies coexist on the control plane.
# Create the referenced integrations with truefoundry_guardrail_group first.
resource "truefoundry_gateway_guardrails_policy" "region" {
  name = "dev-de1-001-gr-frc"

  when = {
    target = {
      model = {
        condition = "in"
        values    = ["dev-de1-001-francecentral/gpt-5-mini"]
      }
    }
  }

  llm_input_guardrails  = ["dev-de1-001-gr-frc/dev-de1-001-cs-frc"]
  llm_output_guardrails = ["dev-de1-001-gr-frc/dev-de1-001-cs-frc"]
  custom_error_message  = "Request blocked by content safety."

  # Omit unused hook lists rather than assigning []. For MCP targets use
  # mcp_tool_pre_invoke_guardrails and/or mcp_tool_post_invoke_guardrails.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique policy name: letters, digits, and hyphens. Changing it replaces the policy.
- `when` (Attributes) Requests this policy applies to; all given parts must match. A target with at least one model, MCP server, or MCP tool condition is required. Use `*` to match all targets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when))

### Optional

- `custom_error_message` (String) Message returned to the caller when a guardrail blocks the request.
- `llm_input_guardrails` (List of String) Guardrails run on the LLM input. References are `<guardrail-group>/<guardrail-config>` names. Omit the attribute (rather than an empty list) when unused.
- `llm_output_guardrails` (List of String) Guardrails run on the LLM output. References are `<guardrail-group>/<guardrail-config>` names. Omit the attribute (rather than an empty list) when unused.
- `mcp_tool_post_invoke_guardrails` (List of String) Guardrails run after MCP tool invocations. References are `<guardrail-group>/<guardrail-config>` names. Omit the attribute (rather than an empty list) when unused.
- `mcp_tool_pre_invoke_guardrails` (List of String) Guardrails run before MCP tool invocations. References are `<guardrail-group>/<guardrail-config>` names. Omit the attribute (rather than an empty list) when unused.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the policy.

Optional:

- `metadata` (Map of String) Request metadata key-value pairs to match.
- `subjects` (Attributes) Matches the calling subject by FQN. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when--subjects))
- `target` (Attributes) Matches the request target; the given conditions are OR-ed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when--target))

Required:

Optional:

- `in` (Set of String) Subject FQNs to match.
- `not_in` (Set of String) Subject FQNs to exclude.

Optional:

- `mcp_tools` (Attributes) Matches MCP tools per server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when--target--mcp_tools))
- `model` (Attributes) Matches the model, as `<provider-account>/<model>` names. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when--target--model))

### Nested Schema for `when.target.mcp_servers`

Required:

### Nested Schema for `when.target.mcp_tools`

Required:

- `condition` (String) Match semantics. One of: `in`, `not_in`.
- `values` (Attributes Set) MCP servers and their covered tools. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--when--target--mcp_tools--values))

### Nested Schema for `when.target.mcp_tools.values`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the MCP server.

Optional:

- `enabled_tools` (Set of String) Specific tools covered when `enable_all_tools` is false.



<a id="nestedatt--when--target--model"></a>
### Nested Schema for `when.target.model`

Required:

- `values` (Set of String) Values to match against.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import truefoundry_gateway_guardrails_policy.region dev-de1-001-gr-frc
```
